threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the train apps for delays instead of just expecting them. Everyone else knows it's part of the experience.
Caught the 333 last night; a guy was singing opera while the driver pretended he didn’t hear. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I found half the people on my street were attending the same spontaneous street party, sharing food and laughter. That's Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how some cafes here will serve you a shot of espresso and a glass of sparkling water for the same price? It's like a mini service ceremony. Love it!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows that avoiding BART during rush hour is just as important as knowing the best taqueria for those late-night cravings.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 line at 4pm, and the driver announced a spontaneous dance-off after a tech guy spilled his coffee. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals actually use them for quick chats and grabbing a croissant from the baker.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for directions at the Placa del Sol instead of just following their phone’s GPS while clutching a coffee.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line' and ask for the 'quickest route' instead of embracing the chaos.
Last night on the 35, a guy argued with his reflection in the window for a solid 20 minutes. Brixton at midnight, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when the neighbor's parrot started mimicking the U-Bahn announcements—perfectly. That was my wake-up call.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find currywurst stalls that open at 6 AM, serving drunchies to night owls and early risers alike. It's a local rite of passage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you're a local when you navigate the BART delays like a pro, but still refuse to touch Muni after they left you waiting with a dog on the tracks.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a full Muni car stop to let a raccoon wander across the street. The passengers didn’t bat an eye. Just another day in the city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is only about fancy cafés; they miss the local bakeries where the real morning magic happens. Fresh pa de pessic is a must.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their still-fresh appreciation for the magic of the light bouncing off the buildings at sunset—like they’ve never seen anything quite like it.
